title: TypeScript SDK: bidi async-iterator <-> WebStreams adapter + robust retry patterns
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and implement a lightweight, well-documented adapter in the TypeScript SDK that enables bidirectional interoperability between async iterators (AsyncGenerator) used by SDK consumers and Web Streams (ReadableStream/TransformStream) used in browser fetch and some Node runtimes. Include a production-ready retry strategy for transient network interruptions that preserves ordering, supports resume tokens where available, and exposes ergonomic cancellation/backpressure controls to app developers.
background: There are multiple existing tickets and ad-hoc implementations in app code that attempt to bridge SDK streaming responses between async-iterators and Web Streams APIs. Customers and example repos exercise both patterns (for server and browser). Current SDK exposes streaming as an AsyncIterator in Node, and as a browser ReadableStream in web bundles, but developers frequently need to convert between the two and handle transient network errors. Existing Linear docs (ENG-4721, ENG-6183, ENG-7329, ENG-8391, ENG-9142) cover parts of ergonomics and adapters but do not provide a single, well-tested, retry-aware bridge supporting resume semantics, configurable backpressure strategies, or bidi streaming (client-to-server and server-to-client) scenarios. This causes duplicated code in examples, inconsistent cancellation semantics, and brittle retry logic in integrations.
proposed_solution: Add a new module in the TypeScript SDK: sdk/streaming/bridge.ts (exported as StreamBridge). The module will provide: 1) toWebStream(iterable, options): converts an AsyncIterable<ResponseChunk> into a ReadableStream with proper backpressure and AbortSignal handling. 2) fromWebStream(webStream, options): converts a ReadableStream into an AsyncIterable. 3) wrapStreamingCall(fetchFn, options): high-level helper that calls the backend and yields parsed messages while implementing retry-on-idempotent-segment with resume token support. 4) RetryPolicy helper implementing exponential backoff + jitter and max-attempts, with hooks for custom retryable rules. 5) Tests and examples demonstrating bidi piping (client request stream -> SDK upload stream, server response stream -> AsyncIterator consumer). Options surfaces include: concurrencyLimit, highWaterMark, idleResumeTimeout, retryPolicyName, resumeTokenHeader, idempotencyKey. Integrate AbortSignal, event hooks (onRetry, onResume, onChunk), and metrics hooks to Redwood Console (counters/timings). The implementation will favor WHATWG streams primitives so it works in modern Node (>=18) and browsers; for older Node we'll include a tiny compatibility shim documented and exported as nodeCompat().
acceptance_criteria: 1) Public API exported: StreamBridge.toWebStream, StreamBridge.fromWebStream, and wrapStreamingCall documented in SDK docs. 2) Unit tests covering conversion directions, abort/cancellation, backpressure behavior, and retry decisions. 3) Integration tests exercising browser fetch ReadableStream + Node AsyncIterator conversion in CI. 4) Retry tests simulate transient 502/ECONNRESET and verify correct resume (where server sends resume tokens) or safe restart with order guarantees when resume unavailable. 5) Example apps updated (examples/streams-bidi and examples/browser-streams) and a sample PR merged. 6) Performance regression <= 5% tail latency for typical small-chunk workloads compared to previous baseline. 7) API compatibility: import paths stable for 1 minor release cycle; deprecation notes included if needed.
backward_compatibility: Default SDK behavior unchanged for existing users. The new module is additive. We will not change existing stream response shapes. The high-level helper wrapStreamingCall is opt-in; tests will ensure no global behavior changes. If we later want to switch defaults, we will follow deprecation policy and include upgrade guide.
risks:
- Resume token spec heterogeneity: backend must produce resume tokens consistently; fallback behavior needs to be defensively implemented.
- Backpressure mismatch between producer and consumer could cause memory growth if misconfigured by user. Provide safe defaults.
- Browser/Node differences: WHATWG streams API differences require careful shims and test matrix across Node 16/18+, Chromium-based browsers, and Safari.
- Complexity of bidi flows: need to document ordering guarantees and idempotency assumptions to avoid app-level data duplication on retries.
test_plan: Unit tests for adapter conversions (node-only + browser env via jsdom/playwright).
Fault-injection tests: inject network resets and validate retry counts, resume behavior, and no item duplication when resume token present.
Backpressure stress tests: use a producer that emits 10k small chunks and verify memory remains bounded with default highWaterMark.
End-to-end example tests in examples/streams-bidi (CI job using Playwright to run browser example).
Benchmark job comparing tail latency and throughput vs baseline; run on dedicated CI GPU/VM with identical run script.
Documentation smoke tests: sample code in README builds and lints in both browser and node bundles.
rollout_plan: Merge feature branch behind feature flag 'ts-sdk.streaming.bridge' and release to canary channel.
Run canary e2e suite for 72 hours; monitor errors and streaming-related metrics (abort rates, retry counts, resume success rate).
Collect feedback from Solutions Engineers running customer demos for 2 weeks; address ergonomics bugs as hotfixes.
Flip flag for stable release once canary is green and performance targets met. Publish migration guide and changelog entry.
Post-release: run customer-facing docs push with examples and a short migration/usage guide.
Plan follow-up: add higher-level server-side helpers for gRPC-like bidi if there is demand.
notes: Prefer WHATWG streams API surface to minimize branching across runtimes. Keep the public surface minimal and ergonomic: most users should never touch retry hooks unless they need extreme control.
